title: Resume reuses a worktree base that main has moved past — cycle 1628 shipped into GIT_FF_MERGE_DIVERGED after 11 phases
details: Cycle 1628 was checkpointed at scout on a quota exit (exit 85) with worktree_base_sha=21d710cd already stamped in cycle-state.json. While the loop was idle the plane advanced (three PR merges synced onto main). `evolve loop --resume` reused the checkpoint without re-validating the base: the builder committed 729 lines on top of 21d710cd, audit passed after one repair, and the atomic ship's ff-merge precondition refused with GIT_FF_MERGE_DIVERGED (rc=128, divergent history); the continuation classifier saw conflicts (verdict=2) and did not stamp a resume, so 11 phases of work were lost from the ship path and the cycle ended FAIL. Fix the class, not the instance: at resume, compare the checkpoint's worktree_base_sha with main; when main has advanced and the worktree has no commits yet (a scout/triage checkpoint), re-provision or rebase the worktree onto main before dispatch; when it has commits, route through the existing ship-recovery rebase (ship_recovery.go) instead of aborting at the precondition. Acceptance: a resume test that advances main after the checkpoint is written and asserts the cycle ships (ff succeeds) or routes through recovery; the ORCHESTRATOR_PHASE_ABORTED reason for GIT_FF_MERGE_DIVERGED never appears for a resumed cycle whose base is an ancestor of main. Operator-side rule recorded meanwhile: after a quota exit that left a checkpoint, `evolve cycle reset` before syncing the plane.
